q: Biodiversity ensures natural ____ for all life on the earth, for example, abundant crops and fresh air.
e: Biodiversity ensures natural sustainability for all life on the earth, for example, abundant crops and fresh air. Write sustainability in the gap.

q: More than 3 billion people depend on marine and coastal biodiversity, while more than 1.6 billion people rely on ____ for their livelihoods.
e: More than 3 billion people depend on marine and coastal biodiversity, while more than 1.6 billion people rely on forests for their livelihoods. Write forests in the gap.

q: The loss of biodiversity affects the lives of more than 1 billion people living in ____ lands.
e: The loss of biodiversity affects the lives of more than 1 billion people living in dry lands. That missing piece is dry.

q: Ecosystems and species are being lost at an alarming rate, not just by the direct action of humans, but also indirectly as a result of climate ____.
e: Ecosystems and species are being lost at an alarming rate, not just by the direct action of humans, but also indirectly as a result of climate change. Write change in the gap.

q: There are five major threats to biodiversity: habitat loss and the degradation of the environment, climate change, excessive use of fertilizers and pollution, overexploitation, and invasive ____ species.
e: There are five major threats to biodiversity: habitat loss and the degradation of the environment, climate change, excessive use of fertilizers and pollution, overexploitation, and invasive alien species. That missing piece is alien.

q: Habitat ____ has played a key role in extinction.
e: Habitat destruction has played a key role in extinction. That missing piece is destruction.

q: The clearing of land for agriculture, housing, transport, leisure facilities and industry removes ____.
e: The clearing of land for agriculture, housing, transport, leisure facilities and industry removes vegetation. The blank is vegetation.

q: Consequently, many species of plants and animals either lose their habitats completely or their habitats become divided into small areas, which is known as habitat ____.
e: Consequently, many species of plants and animals either lose their habitats completely or their habitats become divided into small areas, which is known as habitat fragmentation. That missing piece is fragmentation.

q: Factors causing habitat destruction are overpopulation, deforestation, pollution and global ____.
e: Factors causing habitat destruction are overpopulation, deforestation, pollution and global warming. The blank is warming.

q: Habitat size and number of species are systematically ____.
e: Habitat size and number of species are systematically related. That missing piece is related.

q: Physically larger species and those living at lower latitudes or in forests or oceans are more sensitive to reduction in habitat ____.
e: Physically larger species and those living at lower latitudes or in forests or oceans are more sensitive to reduction in habitat area. That missing piece is area.

q: Shifting cultivation in upland areas, gold mining, urbanization and the clearance of natural forests for agricultural expansion are examples of land-use ____ in Myanmar.
e: Shifting cultivation in upland areas, gold mining, urbanization and the clearance of natural forests for agricultural expansion are examples of land-use change in Myanmar. The blank is change.

q: Habitat loss occurs when natural environments are transformed or modified to serve human ____.
e: Habitat loss occurs when natural environments are transformed or modified to serve human needs. Write needs in the gap.

q: Habitat loss is the most significant cause of biodiversity loss ____.
e: Habitat loss is the most significant cause of biodiversity loss globally. The blank is globally.

q: Factors such as the replacement of local landraces with modern varieties, agricultural area expansion, overgrazing, dams and canal construction and urbanization are major threats to the ____ of Myanmar.
e: Factors such as the replacement of local landraces with modern varieties, agricultural area expansion, overgrazing, dams and canal construction and urbanization are major threats to the agrobiodiversity of Myanmar. Write agrobiodiversity in the gap.

q: Pollution (soil, water or air) is a growing threat on both land and in ____ ecosystems.
e: Pollution (soil, water or air) is a growing threat on both land and in aquatic ecosystems. Write aquatic in the gap.

q: Pollution is caused by uncontrolled pesticide and herbicide uses, various factory wastes, different kinds of rubbish, human sewage, radioactive materials and industrial ____.
e: Pollution is caused by uncontrolled pesticide and herbicide uses, various factory wastes, different kinds of rubbish, human sewage, radioactive materials and industrial wastes. The blank is wastes.

q: Little is known about the status of invasive alien species in Myanmar, but a few ____ have been observed in the country.
e: Little is known about the status of invasive alien species in Myanmar, but a few IAS have been observed in the country. Write IAS in the gap.

q: IAS can also be introduced unintentionally by tourists or through the transport of cargo or movement of pets, plant parts and ____.
e: IAS can also be introduced unintentionally by tourists or through the transport of cargo or movement of pets, plant parts and seeds. The blank is seeds.

q: Some may be intentionally imported for use in research, manufacture of medicine or ornamental and industrial ____.
e: Some may be intentionally imported for use in research, manufacture of medicine or ornamental and industrial uses. The blank is uses.

q: Genetic pollution indicates the loss of identity of wild plant species as a result of transfer of genes from ____ plants.
e: Genetic pollution indicates the loss of identity of wild plant species as a result of transfer of genes from crop plants. Write crop in the gap.

q: Gene flow is expected to have its greatest effect on weed species that are closely related to crop plants taxonomically, ecologically and in their reproductive ____.
e: Gene flow is expected to have its greatest effect on weed species that are closely related to crop plants taxonomically, ecologically and in their reproductive biology. That missing piece is biology.

q: The introduction of genetically engineered (GE) organisms into the complex ecosystems of our environment is a dangerous global experiment with nature and ____.
e: The introduction of genetically engineered (GE) organisms into the complex ecosystems of our environment is a dangerous global experiment with nature and evolution. The blank is evolution.

q: Genetic pollution is undesirable gene flow into ____ populations.
e: Genetic pollution is undesirable gene flow into wild populations. Write wild in the gap.

q: Wind, rain, birds, bees, and insect pollinators have begun carrying genetically altered pollen into adjoining fields, polluting the DNA of crops of organic and non-GE ____.
e: Wind, rain, birds, bees, and insect pollinators have begun carrying genetically altered pollen into adjoining fields, polluting the DNA of crops of organic and non-GE farmers. That missing piece is farmers.

q: Overexploitation, also called ____, can lead to the destruction of the resource, as it will be unable to replenish.
e: Overexploitation, also called overharvesting, can lead to the destruction of the resource, as it will be unable to replenish. The blank is overharvesting.

q: Overfishing is the removal of a species of fish from a body of water at a rate greater than that the species can ____ its population naturally.
e: Overfishing is the removal of a species of fish from a body of water at a rate greater than that the species can replenish its population naturally. That missing piece is replenish.

q: Overfishing can occur in water bodies of any sizes, such as ponds, wetlands, rivers, lakes or oceans, and can result in resource ____.
e: Overfishing can occur in water bodies of any sizes, such as ponds, wetlands, rivers, lakes or oceans, and can result in resource depletion. The blank is depletion.

q: Overlogging is a form of overexploitation caused by legal or illegal logging activities that lead to unsustainable or irrecoverable ____.
e: Overlogging is a form of overexploitation caused by legal or illegal logging activities that lead to unsustainable or irrecoverable deforestation. That missing piece is deforestation.

q: Overhunting threatens one-third of endangered ____, as well as other groups.
e: Overhunting threatens one-third of endangered vertebrates, as well as other groups. The blank is vertebrates.

q: Excluding edible fish, the illegal trade in wildlife is valued at ____ billion per year.
e: Excluding edible fish, the illegal trade in wildlife is valued at \10$ billion per year. The blank is \10$.

q: Bushmeat provides increased opportunity for transmission of several zoonotic viruses from animal hosts to humans, such as Ebola virus and ____.
e: Bushmeat provides increased opportunity for transmission of several zoonotic viruses from animal hosts to humans, such as Ebola virus and HIV. That missing piece is HIV.

q: Climate change is a growing threat to biodiversity because it alters the climate patterns and ____ in which species have evolved.
e: Climate change is a growing threat to biodiversity because it alters the climate patterns and ecosystems in which species have evolved. That missing piece is ecosystems.

q: Rising ocean temperatures and diminishing Arctic sea ice affects marine biodiversity and can shift vegetation ____, having global implications.
e: Rising ocean temperatures and diminishing Arctic sea ice affects marine biodiversity and can shift vegetation zones, having global implications. Write zones in the gap.

q: An increase in the world's population will cause additional strains on ____.
e: An increase in the world's population will cause additional strains on resources. Write resources in the gap.

q: An increase in population will inevitably create pressures leading to more deforestation, decreased biodiversity, and spikes in pollution and ____.
e: An increase in population will inevitably create pressures leading to more deforestation, decreased biodiversity, and spikes in pollution and emissions. The blank is emissions.

q: Wildlife trade refers to the commerce of products that are derived from non-domesticated animals or plants usually extracted from their natural environment or raised under controlled ____.
e: Wildlife trade refers to the commerce of products that are derived from non-domesticated animals or plants usually extracted from their natural environment or raised under controlled conditions. Write conditions in the gap.

q: Illegal wildlife trade contributes directly to the loss of species and habitat ____.
e: Illegal wildlife trade contributes directly to the loss of species and habitat destruction. Write destruction in the gap.

q: The most trafficked animal in the world is the ____, accounting for as much as $20\%$ of all illegal wildlife trade.
e: The most trafficked animal in the world is the pangolin, accounting for as much as 20\% of all illegal wildlife trade. The blank is pangolin.

q: The most trafficked animal in the world is the pangolin, accounting for as much as ____ of all illegal wildlife trade.
e: The most trafficked animal in the world is the pangolin, accounting for as much as 20\% of all illegal wildlife trade. Write 20\% in the gap.

q: Pangolins are the only ____ mammal on earth.
e: Pangolins are the only scaly mammal on earth. Write scaly in the gap.

q: Wildlife smuggling may also cause the introduction of invasive and harmful species into an ecosystem, putting a strain on resources through interspecific ____.
e: Wildlife smuggling may also cause the introduction of invasive and harmful species into an ecosystem, putting a strain on resources through interspecific competition. Write competition in the gap.

q: The illegal wildlife trade has been linked to the emergence and spread of new infectious diseases in humans, including emergent ____.
e: The illegal wildlife trade has been linked to the emergence and spread of new infectious diseases in humans, including emergent viruses. The blank is viruses.

q: National and international laws are in place for wildlife protection, such as CITES and Conservation of Biodiversity and Protected Areas Law (____) in Myanmar.
e: National and international laws are in place for wildlife protection, such as CITES and Conservation of Biodiversity and Protected Areas Law (2018) in Myanmar. The blank is 2018.
